wording: ## Who this applies to
disposition: Heading; all operative amounts/methods have separate bound rows.

disposition: bound

wording: - **Not here: letting that belongs to another kind of income** (§ 21(3) EStG). Property held in a business, a trading partnership, or a trade in property (gewerblicher Grundstückshandel) is taxed as business income: refer, and see `de-trade-tax`. Hotel-like services can also make a let a trade.
disposition: Bound category rule and source-backed hotel-style referral; not a categorical trade determination.

wording: - **Residents.** A person with a home or habitual abode in Germany is taxed on worldwide income. This skill computes the German rental result. Rent from property abroad (Anlage AUS, treaty exemption): refer.
disposition: bound residence/scope; foreign-treaty computation is explicit referral

wording: - **Non-residents with German property** are taxed on German rent under [§ 49(1) no. 6 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__49.html). Compute the rental result with this skill, then go to `de-non-resident-tax` for liability, the tariff and filing.
disposition: bound

wording: - **Year.** Tax year 2026, the calendar year. The consolidated EStG as read applies "erstmals für den Veranlagungszeitraum 2026" ([§ 52(1) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__52.html)). For 2025 returns still being filed, see "Deadlines and filing".
disposition: bound

wording: - **Measure.** Receipts less Werbungskosten, on a cash basis. The result joins the client's other income at the normal tariff with solidarity surcharge and church tax: use `de-einkommensteuer-freelancer` for the tariff.
disposition: bound measure; full tariff belongs to sibling

wording: - **Refer, not covered here**: co-ownership determinations (separate and uniform assessment), heirs' communities, funds, usufruct (Nießbrauch), heritable building rights (Erbbaurecht) as a party, §§ 7h and 7i, and §§ 15a and 15b loss limits.
disposition: Declared excluded/specialist scope; not a substantive outcome.

wording: ## The taxable base
disposition: Heading; all operative amounts/methods have separate bound rows.

wording: ### Income and timing
disposition: Heading; all operative amounts/methods have separate bound rows.

wording: - **Income**: rent; Umlagen (running costs paid by the tenant); settlement back-payments; a deposit kept and set off against rent, running costs or damage; payments for antenna, wind or Wi-Fi sites; a furniture surcharge; VAT received on an opted let; grants for rent (2025 instructions, lines 13 to 31). A refundable deposit is not income while held.
disposition: Bound actual receipts/deposit treatment; furniture consideration is an application of paid rental-use income, not an imputed charge.

wording: - **Umlagen count twice**: income when received; the running costs paid are Werbungskosten.
disposition: bound

wording: - **Cash basis** ([§ 11 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__11.html)): income when received, costs when paid. Regularly recurring items paid shortly before or after the turn of the year belong to the year they relate to. Rent received in advance for a let of more than five years **may** be spread over the period; costs paid in advance for more than five years **must** be spread. A market-level loan discount (Disagio) is deductible when paid.
disposition: bound

wording: ### Werbungskosten ([§ 9 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__9.html))
disposition: Heading; all operative amounts/methods have separate bound rows.

wording: Costs "zur Erwerbung, Sicherung und Erhaltung der Einnahmen", deductible in the year paid, only for a property that earns or is intended to earn rent. Never for a flat the client lives in or lets free.
disposition: bound

wording: - **Deductible**: loan interest so far as linked to the property, and the cost of raising the loan (§ 9(1) no. 1); property tax, other public charges and building insurance (no. 2); AfA and § 7b (no. 7); liability insurance; running costs, including those passed on; Hausgeld **except** the maintenance-reserve part, which is deductible only when the owners' association spends it; management; the tax adviser's rental share; tenancy legal fees; advertising and the broker for finding a tenant; rent-account fees; maintenance.
disposition: Bound income-related cost categories. Incidental management/legal/advertising/account fees are writer applications of9(1), not assertions of automatic deductibility without the income connection.

wording: - **Travel**: actual cost, or 30 cents per km **driven** by car (§ 9(1) no. 4a and § 9(3) EStG with [§ 5(2) BRKG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/brkg_2005/__5.html)). If the property were a first place of activity, the commuting allowance of EUR 0.38 per full km one way applies instead. When a let property is one is not settled on the pages read: ask the accountant.
disposition: bound for numeric rule; actual first-place determination explicitly unconfirmed

wording: - **Not deductible**: loan principal (Tilgung); transfer tax, notary and broker on the purchase (they go into acquisition cost); reserve payments until spent; own-use or free flats; the unpaid part of a cheap let; fines (§ 9(5) with § 4(5) no. 8 EStG); income tax, solidarity surcharge and church tax.
disposition: Bound applications of interest-versus-acquisition/private-cost rules. Principal is distinguished from interest; exceptional economic-benefit disgorgement is not decided by the generic fine exclusion. Church-tax special-expense treatment is outside this rental-cost list.

wording: - **§ 35c energy credit**: only for a building used **only** for the owner's own housing ([§ 35c(2) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__35c.html)), and not for costs deducted as Werbungskosten (§ 35c(3)). For a let property, energy works are maintenance or production cost under the rules below, never the § 35c credit.
disposition: bound

wording: ### Building depreciation (AfA, [§ 7 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__7.html))
disposition: Heading; all operative amounts/methods have separate bound rows.

wording: - **Completion date decides the straight-line rate**, not the purchase date: 3% after 2022, 2% for 1925 to 2022, 2.5% before 1925 (§ 7(4) sentence 1 no. 2). This covers every privately held building, housing or not, including flats and separate parts of a building (§ 7(5b)). The separate 3% rate in no. 1 is for business-asset buildings not used for housing: never use it for a private shop or office completed before 2023.
disposition: bound

wording: - **Shorter actual life.** If the actual life is under 33 years (after 2022), 50 years (1925 to 2022) or 40 years (before 1925), that life may be used (§ 7(4) sentence 2). The 2025 instructions call this an exceptional case that must be proved to the tax office. Refer.
disposition: bound

wording: - **Older staged rates.** A building built or bought in its completion year under an application or contract before 1 January 2006 (housing; earlier dates for the other historic branches) may be on the staged rates of § 7(5). Ask what past returns used; refer any change.
disposition: bound afterDE-L22 restoration

wording: - **Acquired free of charge** (gift or inheritance): continue the previous owner's rate (2025 instructions).
disposition: bound

wording: - **Declining-balance AfA, § 7(5a).** Instead of 3% straight-line, 5% of the remaining value ("Restwert") each year, so far as the building is used for **housing**, if all hold: it is in Germany, the EU or the EEA; the client built it, or bought it by the end of the completion year; and construction started (the date on the construction-start notice required by state law; where none is required, the client declares a voluntary notice) or the binding purchase contract was made after 30 September 2023 and before 1 October 2029. No extraordinary write-down while it runs. Switching to straight-line is allowed, then on the remaining value and remaining life.
disposition: bound

wording: - **Base.** Price plus side costs (transfer tax, notary, land register, the buyer's broker) under [§ 255 HGB](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/hgb/__255.html), less the land share. Land is never depreciated. A maintenance reserve bought with a flat is excluded (2025 instructions). Grants reduce the base (line 89). A former own home let for the first time needs a first computation.
disposition: bound

wording: - **Price split.** Split by the ratio of market values, not by the residual-value method (2025 instructions). The [BMF purchase-price split tool](https://www.bundesfinanzministerium.de/Content/DE/Downloads/Steuern/Berechnung-Aufteilung-Grundstueckskaufpreis.html) makes or tests a split. A contract split at arm's length or an expert valuation may also be used; the tax office may challenge a high building share.
disposition: Bound market-value/contract/expert principles plus explicitly identified official work-aid web observation; no2026work-aid execution.

wording: - **First-year month cut.** Cut one twelfth for each full month before the month of acquisition or completion (§ 7(1) sentence 4). Statute applies it to § 7(5a) (sentence 5). For straight-line AfA, the BMF letter of 21 May 2025 on § 7b says so too: "bei Fertigstellung nach dem 31. Januar wäre eine zeitanteilige Kürzung der linearen AfA im Jahr der Fertigstellung erforderlich" (example 7). Only the old staged § 7(5) rates take a full first year.
disposition: bound

wording: - **For example**: completed February 2026, bought with benefit and burden from 1 April 2026, building share EUR 300,000. Declining-balance: 300,000 × 5% × 9/12 = EUR 11,250 in 2026; 2027: (300,000 − 11,250) × 5% = EUR 14,437.50. Straight-line instead: 300,000 × 3% × 9/12 = EUR 6,750. The binding contract was made in March 2026. Total acquisition cost is EUR 400,000, including land of EUR 100,000. From April, rent is EUR 1,200 plus Umlagen of EUR 250 a month: income is 9 × (1,200 + 250) = EUR 13,050. Interest of EUR 9,000, running costs of EUR 2,250 and management of EUR 600 total EUR 11,850. The declining-balance loss is 13,050 − 11,850 − 11,250 = EUR 10,050; with straight-line AfA the loss is EUR 5,550.
disposition: arithmetic controls; selected clauses bound

wording: - **End**: until fully written off, or the year of sale.
disposition: Bound ordinary cessation inference from own depreciable asset/rental use; exact month-of-sale AfA expressly remains unconfirmed.

wording: ### § 7b special depreciation for new rental flats ([§ 7b EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__7b.html))
disposition: Heading; all operative amounts/methods have separate bound rows.

wording: Up to 5% of the base in the year of acquisition or production and the three following years, on top of normal AfA under § 7(4) or § 7(5a). All must hold:
disposition: bound

wording: - The building work creates **new** flats that did not exist before, under a building application or notice in the **old window** (after 31 August 2018 and before 1 January 2022) or the **new window** (after 31 December 2022 and before 1 October 2029). Nothing applied for in 2022 qualifies.
disposition: bound

wording: - Cost per m² of living space **not more than** the cliff (EUR 3,000 old window, EUR 5,200 new window), or no § 7b at all. The base is capped per m² (EUR 2,000 old, EUR 4,000 new). Normal AfA still runs on full cost (BMF letter of 21 May 2025, para. 65).
disposition: bound

wording: - In the EU, or a state giving the required administrative help. If bought, bought by the end of the completion year; only the buyer claims.
disposition: bound

wording: - Let **for housing, against payment**, in that year and the **nine** following years. Short-term guest accommodation is not housing (§ 7b(2) no. 3).
disposition: bound

wording: - New window only: the building meets "Effizienzhaus 40" with sustainability class, proven by the "Qualitätssiegel Nachhaltiges Gebäude".
disposition: bound

wording: - **Old window ends with 2026**: claims are allowed "letztmalig für den Veranlagungszeitraum 2026" ([§ 52(15a)](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__52.html)), even if four years have not run. A buyer who started in 2024 claims 2024 to 2026 and loses the fourth year (BMF letter, para. 16, example 1). The new window has no such end.
disposition: bound

wording: - **Claw-back** of all past claims if the flat is not let for housing for ten years, is sold in that time with the gain untaxed, or later costs push it over the cliff within three years after the year of acquisition or production (§ 7b(4)).
disposition: bound

wording: - **After four years**, AfA runs on the remaining value ([§ 7a(9) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__7a.html); BMF letter, para. 66). Refer the computation.
disposition: bound

wording: - **De minimis aid**: for the new window, only claimants with farming, business or self-employed income must meet the EU de minimis rules (§ 7b(5)); the 2025 instructions treat the old window as de minimis aid and ask for the other aid received.
disposition: bound

wording: - **For example**: an 80 m² flat applied for in 2024, completed and bought January 2026, Effizienzhaus 40 with the seal, let long-term, cost of the flat without land EUR 400,000 (land never enters § 7b: BMF letter, para. 43). 400,000 / 80 = EUR 5,000 per m², not over 5,200: qualifies. Base cap 80 × 4,000 = EUR 320,000; § 7b 320,000 × 5% = EUR 16,000 a year for 2026 to 2029, plus straight-line 400,000 × 3% = EUR 12,000 (January, no cut). At EUR 420,000 (EUR 5,250 per m²) there is no § 7b.
disposition: bound plus arithmetic controls

wording: Source for the letter: [BMF letter of 21 May 2025 on § 7b EStG](https://www.bundesfinanzministerium.de/Content/DE/Downloads/BMF_Schreiben/Steuerarten/Einkommensteuer/2025-05-21-anwendungsschreiben-7b-estg-neu.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5).
disposition: Pointer to the actual bound official letter/handbook quotations.

wording: ### Maintenance or production cost
disposition: Heading; all operative amounts/methods have separate bound rows.

wording: - **Maintenance** (Erhaltungsaufwand) keeps or restores the condition: repainting, like-for-like heating, roof repair, equivalent windows. Deductible when paid, or spread under § 82b EStDV.
disposition: Bound maintenance principle and stated examples; fact-sensitive production/acquisition/15percent gates are retained in adjacent paragraphs.

wording: - **Production cost** creates something new, extends, or substantially improves beyond the original condition ([§ 255(2) HGB](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/hgb/__255.html)): balcony, attic conversion, lift, lifting the standard (judged mainly by heating, sanitary and electrical installations and windows). The 2025 instructions: works that bring the flat or building "auf einen höheren Standard" are production or acquisition cost. Capitalised and depreciated with the building.
disposition: bound

wording: - **Bought in a poor state**: making non-working essential parts work again (defective heating, water or fire damage), and change-of-use works before first use, are **acquisition** cost (2025 instructions).
disposition: bound

wording: - **The 15% rule, acquisition-related production cost** ([§ 6(1) no. 1a EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__6.html), applied to Werbungskosten by § 9(5) sentence 2). Repair and modernisation works carried out **within three years** of acquisition become production cost if their total cost **without VAT** "15 Prozent der Anschaffungskosten des Gebäudes übersteigen". It is a cliff: over it, **all** of them are capitalised. The three years are added up, so a later job can pull earlier deductions back in. Exactly 15% is not over. Not counted: extensions, and maintenance that usually recurs every year, such as servicing.
disposition: bound

wording: - **For example**: building completed 1970, bought May 2025, building share EUR 200,000, so the limit is EUR 30,000. Works without VAT: EUR 12,000 in 2025 (deducted on the 2025 return) and EUR 19,000 in 2026. Total EUR 31,000 is over EUR 30,000: all of it is production cost, including 2025, and is depreciated at 2% with the building: EUR 31,000 × 2% = EUR 620 for a full year. Refer the correction of the 2025 assessment. With 2026 works of EUR 18,000 the total is exactly EUR 30,000: not over, judge each job on its own.
disposition: arithmetic checked; assessment correction is explicit referral

wording: - **Spreading, [§ 82b EStDV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estdv_1955/__82b.html).** Larger maintenance may be spread evenly over two to five years if, **when paid**, the building is not a business asset and is **mainly** housing: housing floor area more than half the usable area; garages count as housing up to one car per flat. On sale, transfer into a business or end of letting, the rest is deducted that year. Co-owners must use the same period. Works in redevelopment areas and on listed buildings (§§ 11a, 11b EStG, §§ 7h, 7i): refer.
disposition: bound; special scheme computation is referral

wording: ### Furniture
disposition: Heading; all operative amounts/methods have separate bound rows.

wording: A furniture surcharge is rent. Furniture and fitted kitchens are depreciated over their useful life (§ 7(1) EStG; lines 42 to 45). An item usable on its own costing not more than EUR 800 net may be deducted at once ([§ 6(2) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__6.html) through § 9(1) no. 7). For the cheap-let comparison, use a furniture adjustment already provided by the local rent index without adding it twice. Otherwise add a surcharge only if it can be established from the local market for furnished lets; if no market value can be determined, no surcharge is added. wording: ### Vacancy, holiday flats and the intention to make a surplus (Liebhaberei)
disposition: Heading; all operative amounts/methods have separate bound rows.

wording: Source for this part: BMF letter of 8 October 2004 (BStBl I p. 933), as printed with its notes in the [official income tax handbook 2024, Anhang 30 II](https://esth.bundesfinanzministerium.de/esth/2024/C-Anhaenge/Anhang-30/II/anhang-30-II.html) ("para." below).
disposition: Pointer to the actual bound official letter/handbook quotations.

wording: - **Long-term home lets.** A let of a flat meant to last is taken to aim at a surplus without a test (para. 1). That presumption does not cover commercial premises or undeveloped land (note to para. 1): there the forecast below decides.
disposition: bound to retained official handbook

wording: - **Signs against the intention** (paras. 5 to 7): a let planned only for a time (a fixed-term lease with stated own use or sale, short financing, an early search for a buyer), or a sale or own use within about five years of acquisition with only losses in that time. The client can rebut by showing the decision to sell or move in came later (para. 9).
disposition: bound

wording: - **Vacancy.** Costs are deductible before the first let and during a gap once the decision to let for good is made and shown by serious, continuing efforts (agent, advertisements, a realistic rent) (paras. 25 to 27). The client carries the proof. Without such efforts, or if the flat cannot be let in the foreseeable future, the intention lapses and costs stop (notes to para. 26).
disposition: bound

wording: - **Forms.** A holiday flat, or any object let **short-term** (for example through an online platform), needs **Anlage V-FeWo** as well as Anlage V (2025 instructions). Each V-FeWo form covers up to four flats.
disposition: bound

wording: - **Day counts** where the owner used it, left it free to others, or could use it at any time: days of own use (including free use by others; not short stays for servicing, cleaning, renovation or checks), letting and vacancy. Own use possible at any time: split vacancy by the ratio of own use to letting. Own use limited to set times (for example let through an agent): only the reserved time is own use, and vacancy counts as letting. Never used by the owner and let only to changing guests: give the letting days usual in that place, from tourist office or municipal records.
disposition: bound

wording: - **Holiday flat let only to changing guests** and otherwise held ready for them: the intention is taken as given without a test, whether the client lets it directly or through an agent (para. 16). Exception: if letting days fall short of the usual local letting time by **at least 25%**, with no obstacle to letting, a forecast is needed (note to para. 16).
disposition: bound with qualification

wording: - **Proving there is no own use** (para. 17): the client shows one of: letting handed to an unrelated agent with own use excluded by contract for the whole year; the flat is in or right next to the client's own home, which meets the client's needs; the client has more than one holiday flat in the place and uses only one; or letting days at least equal the local seasonal average. Otherwise the client must prove it, and with too few letting days show stronger advertising (para. 18). Short stays for servicing, key handover, cleaning, checks, repairs or owners' meetings are not own use; longer stays or stays with family need explaining (para. 19).
disposition: bound

wording: - **Holiday flat let part of the time and used by the owner** (or reserved for own use, or lent free): the intention is always tested by forecast (para. 21), per flat, not per let (para. 34). Only costs for let days and vacancy allocated to letting go in (para. 39); mixed costs (interest, property charges, maintenance, AfA, insurance) are split by days of each use (para. 40). Vacancy: if own use is limited to set times, only those count as own use; if possible at any time, split vacancy by the ratio of own use to letting; if the extent of own use cannot be established, vacancy is split 50/50 (paras. 22, 23). The forecast then follows para. 34: 30 years, § 7(4) AfA, five-year average, 10% margins (see the cheap-let forecast above).
disposition: bound

wording: - **Without the intention** the losses are not recognised (Liebhaberei). If the lack of intention only shows later, final assessments can be changed under § 173(1) no. 1 AO (para. 10).
disposition: bound
